findings.text: The recommended workstream does not account for an active OpenSpec contract mismatch in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/`. `proposal.md` requires “Add a `--list-lints` subcommand or equivalent diagnostic that prints all available lints with their current effective level,” but `design.md`, `tasks.md`, and `specs/documentation/spec.md` only cover `disabled_lints`/`lint_levels`. Recommending implementation work here without first reconciling that mismatch risks building against an incomplete plan.

The response overstates the repository-state inspection. The supplied evidence does not include a `git status`/branch probe or TODO search, yet the answer claims `main`, “only dirty path `.pi/prompt-history.jsonl`,” and “only code TODO hit was vendored test-support `tests/support/dylint/internal/src/git.rs`.” From the evidence shown, only the diff stat supports that `.pi/prompt-history.jsonl` is modified; branch and TODO claims are not established.

The test-state summary is stronger than the evidence. The only probe shown is `nix develop -c bash -lc 'cargo test --quiet'` stalling on `waiting for the big garbage collector lock...`. That proves the chosen command was blocked by environment state, but it does not prove “not repo code” or establish whether tests are passing/failing once the lock clears.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` has no task for the proposal’s `--list-lints` / “equivalent diagnostic” capability. Evidence: `proposal.md` says “Add a `--list-lints` subcommand or equivalent diagnostic that prints all available lints with their current effective level” and lists new capability `lint-listing`, but no corresponding task appears in `tasks.md`.

The spec-required “warning (not error) for unknown lint names in config” has an implementation task but no verification task. Evidence: `specs/documentation/spec.md` requires “a warning (not error) for unknown lint names in config”; `design.md` Decision 4 says unknown names “produce a warning during config load”; `tasks.md` only includes “Add validation: warn on unknown lint names at load time” and has no test task for warning behavior or non-failure.

The task list is not aligned with the current user request. Evidence: the current prompt narrows work to “Implement `disabled_lints` end-to-end … in `src/config.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, and one fixture-local config test under `ui_tests/`”, but `tasks.md` still plans full-scope `lint_levels`, template/docs updates, `nix flake check`, and Aspen validation. Either the change needs to be split, or the tasks need an explicit phased/deferred boundary so implementers know what is in scope now.

The requested fixture-local config test is under-specified given a known repo failure pattern. Evidence: the current prompt explicitly asks for “one fixture-local config test under `ui_tests/`”; `tasks.md` only says “Integration test: disabled lint produces no diagnostics”; the napkin records that per-fixture `dylint.toml` lookup comes from the fixture source parent and requires a minimal `Cargo.toml` (with empty `[workspace]`) and `src/lib.rs` in the fixture subdirectory. Without encoding that setup in tasks or a check, this test is likely to be implemented incorrectly.

The `lint_levels` implementation path is still ambiguous in design, so the corresponding task is not executable as written. Evidence: `design.md` Decision 2 says to “call `lint_store.register_group_lints` with the appropriate level, or set the lint’s default level during registration”; `tasks.md` says “Implement lint-level override during registration.” The design has not selected one mechanism, so the task lacks a settled target.

The reviewed code completes the `disabled_lints` slice, but the active OpenSpec change is still incomplete. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` still includes unfinished items such as `Add \`lint_levels: HashMap<String, String>\` to \`Config\``, `Unit tests for config parsing with new fields`, `Unit tests for backward compatibility`, and the phase 2/3/4 follow-ons. The reviewed diff only changes `src/config.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `tests/ui.rs`, and `ui_tests/no_unwrap_disabled_custom/`, so this should not be treated as the full `per-lint-configuration` change being done.

`src/lib.rs` introduces a separate hand-maintained `KNOWN_LINTS` string list for validation, while `register_lints` also repeats the same lint names in each `cfg.lint_is_disabled("...")` guard. Evidence: `const KNOWN_LINTS: &[&str] = &[...]` plus the repeated per-lint string literals throughout `src/lib.rs`. This creates two sources of truth that can drift on future lint additions/renames.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/proposal.md` still commits a separate lint-listing feature — “Add a `--list-lints` subcommand or equivalent diagnostic that prints all available lints with their current effective level” and capability `lint-listing` — but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/design.md`, `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md`, and `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` contain no corresponding design, requirement, task, or verification. This is a proposal/design/spec/tasks traceability break that must be resolved before task execution proceeds.

The added requirement in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` says the configuration must include “a warning (not error) for unknown lint names in config,” but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` only has implementation work — “Add validation: warn on unknown lint names at load time” — and no explicit verification task for warning emission or non-fatal behavior. “Unit tests for config parsing with new fields” does not cover that requirement as written.

The requirement text constrains `lint_levels` to `allow`, `warn`, or `deny`, but the current artifacts do not define behavior for invalid values. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/design.md` proposes `lint_levels: HashMap<String, String>` and `tasks.md` mirrors that with “Add `lint_levels: HashMap<String, String>`” plus “Implement lint-level override during registration,” but there is no rule or task for rejecting, warning on, or defaulting invalid strings. Evidence is insufficient to infer the intended behavior, so this needs explicit design/spec clarification.

Verification for per-lint severity is incomplete. `specs/documentation/spec.md` requires a `lint_levels` table mapping lint names to `allow`, `warn`, or `deny`, but `tasks.md` only includes “Integration test: deny-level lint produces error instead of warning.” There is no task to verify `allow` behavior, and no task to verify the effective default/`warn` path.

The validation tasks are underspecified for nix/downstream execution. `tasks.md` says “Verify config changes work in `nix flake check`” and “Test against Aspen with inventory-first lints disabled via config (confirm clean run),” but the napkin records repeated failures when assuming plain `cargo dylint` under nix-managed toolchains and recommends a wrapper path like `scripts/tigerstyle-check.sh`. The current tasks do not name a nix-compatible execution path, so the validation evidence is likely to be flaky or non-reproducible.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/proposal.md` still commits a separate lint-listing feature — “Add a `--list-lints` subcommand or equivalent diagnostic that prints all available lints with their current effective level” plus capability `lint-listing` — but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/design.md`, `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md`, and `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` have no corresponding design, requirement, or task. The cleanup removed backward-compat wording, but the change set remains internally inconsistent.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` still requires “a warning (not error) for unknown lint names in config,” but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` only says “Add validation: warn on unknown lint names at load time” and does not add an explicit verification task for warning emission or non-fatal behavior.

The allowed `lint_levels` values are constrained in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` to `allow`, `warn`, or `deny`, but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/design.md` still models them as `HashMap<String, String>` and does not define behavior for invalid strings. There is no corresponding task in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` to reject, warn on, or default invalid values.

Verification for per-lint severity remains incomplete. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` has only “Integration test: deny-level lint produces error instead of warning”; it does not include verification for `allow` behavior or the default/`warn` path required by the `lint_levels` feature in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md`.

The validation tasks remain underspecified for nix-managed environments. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` says “Verify config changes work in `nix flake check`” and “Test against Aspen...”, but the supplied napkin entries document repeated failures when assuming plain Dylint execution under nix and recommend a wrapper path such as `scripts/tigerstyle-check.sh`. This should stay guidance unless the repo wants a deterministic task-template rule.

`tasks.md` does not include any verification that `disabled_lints` actually prevents registration/pass execution, only that it "produces no diagnostics" (`tasks.md`, Phase 2). That is weaker than the contract in `specs/documentation/spec.md`, which requires `disabled_lints` to "prevent named lints from registering" and in the "Disabling a noisy lint" scenario says "no pass overhead," and weaker than `design.md` Decision 1, which explicitly rejects the alternative of registering the lint at `Allow`. As written, an implementation that merely suppresses diagnostics could satisfy the current test tasks while violating the spec/design.

The proposal’s testing section requires "fixture-local config cases" (`proposal.md`, Impact → Testing), but `tasks.md` has no explicit task to add a fixture-local `dylint.toml` test or to build the fixture layout needed for local config resolution. The only nearby item is "Verify config changes in `nix flake check` and the targeted UI fixture gate" (Phase 4), which does not trace the required local-config case. This is a known failure pattern in the napkin: per-fixture config lookup depends on a fixture-local `Cargo.toml` with empty `[workspace]` and `src/lib.rs`. Without an explicit task, the change can ship without exercising the consumer-owned config path it is introducing.

`design.md` Risk/Trade-offs says the mitigation for config/source drift is to "document that `dylint.toml` disabled_lints takes precedence over source attributes." `tasks.md` Phase 3 documents warnings/ignored invalid values and downstream rollout mapping, but it does not include that precedence documentation. That leaves a stated design mitigation untracked.

Warning-path coverage is underspecified for unknown lint names. `design.md` Decision 4 covers unknown lint names in both `disabled_lints` and `lint_levels`, and `specs/documentation/spec.md` requires a warning for unknown lint names in config. `tasks.md` only has one generic unit test task: "unknown lint name warns without failing config load." That can leave one of the two config entry points untested.

No artifact resolves overlap between `disabled_lints` and `lint_levels` for the same lint. Evidence: `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/proposal.md` introduces both controls; `design.md` Decision 1 says disabled lints "are not registered with the lint store at all"; Decision 2 says registration consults `lint_levels` for each lint's "effective level"; `tasks.md` includes both "Refactor `register_lints` to check `disabled_lints` before each registration" and "Implement lint-level override during registration" but no requirement, scenario, or task defines which wins when both are set. This is a contract gap that can yield divergent implementations and warning behavior.

The "no pass overhead" claim is not backed by a defined, deterministic verification step. Evidence: `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` says disabled lints produce "no diagnostics and no pass overhead"; `tasks.md` Phase 2 has "Integration test: disabled lint is not registered and adds no pass overhead"; no task adds an observable mechanism such as registration inspection, pass invocation counting, or another measurable surrogate. As written, this task is not small or verifiable.

Source-attribute precedence is only documented, not verified. Evidence: `design.md` Risk / Trade-offs says "`disabled_lints` takes precedence over source attributes" because the lint is never registered; `tasks.md` only includes "Document that `disabled_lints` takes precedence over source-level lint attributes" and has no matching integration/UI test. That leaves a user-visible behavior unguarded.

The fixture-local config discovery task correctly reflects prior repo failure modes and should remain explicit. Evidence: `tasks.md` includes "Fixture-local UI test with local `Cargo.toml`, `dylint.toml`, and `src/lib.rs` proving consumer-owned config is discovered from the fixture root", which matches the napkin guidance about `cargo metadata` rooting config lookup at the fixture parent. Do not collapse this into a generic UI test.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` is not internally traceable on rollout profile terminology. Phase 3 says `Show how starter/boundary/inventory profiles map to config`, and Phase 4 says `Test against Aspen with inventory-first lints disabled via config`. But `proposal.md` only says the Aspen playbook distinguishes `"starter" vs "deferred"` and its example comment says `# Phase 1: only enable boundary-first lints`. `design.md` and `specs/documentation/spec.md` do not define `starter`, `boundary`, `inventory`, or `inventory-first`, nor which lints belong to each. Those tasks are not verifiable as written.

The task set does not require a single source of truth or coverage check for valid lint names, even though Phase 1 requires warning on unknown names and Phase 2 changes registration behavior per lint. Evidence: `tasks.md` includes `Add validation: warn on unknown lint names at load time`, `Refactor register_lints to check disabled_lints before each registration`, and `Implement lint-level override during registration`; `design.md` says `src/lib.rs` currently `unconditionally registers all 26 lints`. Without a canonical lint inventory or a check that validation and registration share the same names, config acceptance can drift from actual registered lints.

The fixture-local config-discovery task is still underspecified against a known repo failure mode. `tasks.md` only says `Fixture-local UI test with local Cargo.toml, dylint.toml, and src/lib.rs proving consumer-owned config is discovered from the fixture root`. The napkin guidance for this repo says per-fixture config discovery needs a minimal `Cargo.toml` with empty `[workspace]`, and standalone UI fixtures should use unscoped lint names. Leaving that implicit makes the task prone to false failures unrelated to per-lint config.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` does not unambiguously trace the spec’s explicit `warn`-override scenario. The task says `Integration test: default level or explicit \`warn\` emits a warning`, which can be satisfied by testing only default behavior, but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` has a distinct normative scenario: `GIVEN [tigerstyle.lint_levels] no_unwrap = "warn" ... THEN it emits a warning`. Split or rewrite this task so the explicit `warn` override is mandatory and independently verifiable.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/design.md` Decision 2 commits to validating `lint_levels` strings at load time and "normaliz[ing] accepted values into an internal enum," but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` only names raw-input and downstream-use tasks: `Add lint_levels: HashMap<String, String> to Config (default empty)` and `Implement lint-level override during registration`. The task list does not explicitly cover the validated/internal representation the design chose, so design-to-task traceability is incomplete.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` adds a new `Fixture-local UI test with local Cargo.toml (including empty [workspace]), dylint.toml, and src/lib.rs...` and later requires `Verify config changes in nix flake check and the targeted UI fixture gate`, but no task constrains how that UI path remains runnable under nix/rustup constraints. The supplied napkin explicitly records prior `dylint_testing` UI failures under nix because it shells out to `rustup which rustc` and had to be made conditional when rustup was unavailable. The verification path is therefore underspecified for the environment the task itself names.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` Phase 4 task `Test against Aspen with inventory-only lints disabled via config using the consumer wrapper/template path (confirm clean run)` is not deterministically verifiable as written. The supplied napkin records recurring Aspen-side drift: downstream validation needed a wrapper script under nix-managed toolchains, and Aspen HEAD should not be treated as the archived starter rollout baseline. Without pinning the wrapper/check path and the Aspen target/revision being exercised, this task should be explicitly routed as human validation or rewritten into a deterministic check.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` still normatively reads as if the new keys are mandatory, which conflicts with the design and tasks that treat them as optional defaulted fields. Evidence: `spec.md` says `The configuration MUST include:` followed by `a disabled_lints list` and `a lint_levels table`, while `design.md` Decision 3 says `New fields use #[serde(default)] and empty-collection defaults` and `tasks.md` Phase 1 says `Add disabled_lints: Vec<String> to Config (default empty)` and `Add lint_levels: HashMap<String, String> to Config (default empty)`. That leaves backward compatibility / omitted-field behavior ambiguous, so the claimed “remaining drifts cleared” is overstated.

The rollout-profile terminology is aligned, but the profiles are still not defined in these OpenSpec artifacts, so the profile-mapping and Aspen validation tasks are not fully self-verifiable. Evidence: `proposal.md` says Aspen uses profiles `such as smoke, boundary-first, and inventory-only`; `design.md` says downstream guidance uses those three named profiles; `tasks.md` requires `Show how smoke, boundary-first, and inventory-only rollout profiles map to config` and `Human validation: rerun Aspen with inventory-only lints disabled via config...`; none of the reviewed files identifies which lints belong to each profile or names a canonical source for that membership.

The task `Deterministic check: config validation and registration stay in sync with the same lint-name inventory` in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` is not concrete enough to be verifiable. `design.md` Decision 5 requires one shared canonical inventory for both validation and registration, but the task does not state the enforcing artifact or pass/fail mechanism. As written, drift prevention is a goal, not an enforceable check.

Phase 4’s task `Human validation: rerun Aspen with inventory-only lints disabled via config using templates/tigerstyle-check.sh (or copied consumer equivalent)` in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` depends on a wrapper path that is not established anywhere else in the supplied artifacts. The napkin guidance says downstream validation under nix-managed toolchains should use a wrapper rather than plain `cargo dylint`, but the current change artifacts do not prove that `templates/tigerstyle-check.sh` exists or is the correct path. The validation step is therefore underspecified from the supplied evidence.

`design.md` Decision 3 requires the new config fields to use empty defaults via `#[serde(default)]`, but `tasks.md` has no explicit test task for the omission case where `disabled_lints` and `lint_levels` are absent from `dylint.toml`. The broad task `Unit tests for config parsing with new fields` may cover it, but the acceptance condition is not explicit.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` adds only one inventory check — `Deterministic check: unit test asserts the shared inventory's lint names are unique and that the lint-name slice passed to config validation is derived from the same inventory used by registration` — but no task proves that the shared inventory is complete for the full shipped lint set. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/design.md` Decision 5 says the inventory must store “every canonical lint name,” and the Context says `src/lib.rs` currently registers “all 26 lints.” If a lint is omitted from `LINT_INVENTORY`, both validation and registration could stay internally consistent while silently dropping that lint, and no listed task would fail.

The Phase 4 Aspen task in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` is not self-contained: `Human validation: copy repo template templates/tigerstyle-check.sh into Aspen (or confirm an Aspen-local wrapper derived from that template), apply the inventory-only profile from docs/downstream-rollout.md, rerun on the pinned Aspen revision recorded in evidence, and confirm a clean run`. The supplied artifacts do not identify where the “pinned Aspen revision” evidence lives, and the current proposal/design/spec evidence does not establish `templates/tigerstyle-check.sh` as part of this change. Napkin guidance supports using a wrapper script, but it does not supply the missing evidence path or resolve the template-path reference.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` requires continuation semantics after bad config entries (`Scenario: Unknown lint name warns and continues` and `Scenario: Invalid lint level warns and keeps default`), but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` only covers warning/non-failure (`Unit test: unknown disabled_lints name warns without failing config load`, `Unit test: unknown lint_levels entry warns without failing config load`, `Unit test: invalid lint_levels value warns and keeps the default lint level`). There is no explicit task proving a mixed config still applies remaining valid `disabled_lints` or `lint_levels` entries after ignoring the bad one.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` requires that omitted `disabled_lints` / `lint_levels` "preserve the existing default lint levels", but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` only schedules `Integration test: default lint level still emits a warning when no override is present`. Because the same task list also introduces `LINT_INVENTORY` and moves all registration through that canonical table, there is no task that proves the refactor preserves default-level metadata across the shipped lint set rather than just one representative warning case. Add a deterministic check or snapshot that records each inventory entry's default level, or equivalent no-override verification tied to the shared inventory.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` Phase 4 says `Verify config changes in nix flake check and the targeted UI fixture gate`, but it omits the repo-specific execution guardrail captured in the napkin: newly added UI fixture files must be staged before trusting `nix flake check`, or the flake source snapshot can exclude them. This is not a spec gap, but the validation task is easy to mis-execute without that note.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` still hardcodes unscoped source-attribute syntax in `Scenario: Disabled lint beats source-level attrs` (`AND source code requests #![deny(no_unwrap)]`), but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/proposal.md` describes consumer source attrs as `#[allow(tigerstyle::...)]`, and `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` limits “using unscoped lint names” to the fixture-local UI test. The artifacts are still inconsistent about whether unscoped names are test-only harness syntax or the documented consumer-facing syntax.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` Phase 4 is more concrete than before, but the wrapper step is still not fully evidenced: it now says `copy repo template templates/tigerstyle-check.sh ... as documented by the check-path recipe in docs/downstream-rollout.md`. In the supplied evidence, the rollout readout names archived evidence like `openspec/changes/archive/2026-04-13-custom-clippy-lints/evidence/aspen-check-path-and-config.txt`, but no supplied evidence shows a `templates/tigerstyle-check.sh` path or that `docs/downstream-rollout.md` contains that recipe. The Aspen validation task is still not fully auditable from the cited artifacts.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` is not synchronized with the observed work. The provided task summary says `0 done, 0 in progress, 40 todo`, but `git status` already shows implementation and test changes in `src/config.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `tests/ui.rs`, and new fixture files under `ui_tests/no_unwrap_disabled_custom/`. That breaks task-to-work traceability at the tasks stage.

Phase 2 includes `Fixture-local UI test with local Cargo.toml (including empty [workspace]), dylint.toml, and src/lib.rs...` and `Keep UI/config verification on the repo custom UI harness / checks.ui path`, which matches several prior repo lessons, but it does not explicitly restate the sandbox constraint from the napkin that temporary cargo projects used under nix/crane checks must avoid pulling new dependencies outside the vendored source set. Evidence is limited to the task text in `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` and the 2026-04-14 napkin entry about the crane/nextest sandbox.

The tasks stage is not ready to advance because the spec’s per-lint severity path is still largely unexecuted. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` requires `lint_levels` support plus `allow`/`warn`/`deny` behavior, but `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` still leaves these core tasks open: “Add `lint_levels: HashMap<String, String>`…”, “Normalize validated `lint_levels` values into an internal representation…”, “Implement lint-level override during registration”, and the integration tests for “`allow` level suppresses diagnostics”, “explicit `warn` level emits a warning”, “default lint level still emits a warning when no override is present”, and “`deny` level produces an error instead of a warning”. The change cannot clear the tasks gate while a required capability remains only partially implemented and partially verified.

Registration work is marked done before the design’s anti-drift constraint is in place. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/design.md` Decision 5 says config validation and registration must derive lint names from “one shared inventory.” But `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` still shows “Introduce a shared `LINT_INVENTORY`…”, “Eliminate out-of-band lint registration wiring…”, “Refactor config validation and registration to derive accepted lint names from that shared inventory…”, and both inventory deterministic checks as TODO, while “Refactor `register_lints` to check `disabled_lints` before each registration” is already marked done. That sequencing leaves the design’s sole-source-of-truth requirement unmet and should block more registration/config work until the inventory and checks land.

Required verification and rollout closure work remains open across warning semantics, precedence semantics, and downstream validation. `spec.md` requires warnings for unknown lint names, invalid levels, and disabled-vs-level conflicts, plus the “Disabled lint beats source-level attrs” scenario. `tasks.md` still leaves the warning-path unit tests, “Unit test: overlap between `disabled_lints` and `lint_levels` warns and keeps the lint disabled”, “Integration test: disabled lint stays inert even when `lint_levels` tries to raise it”, and “Integration test: disabled lint stays inert even when source-level attrs try to raise it” as TODO. In addition, proposal/design-aligned closure tasks remain open in Phase 3/4, including template/docs updates, “Verify config changes in `nix flake check` and the targeted UI fixture gate…”, and the Aspen reconstruction task. Those open items mean the change lacks full verification traceability for the documented behavior and known rollout failure modes.

The final response overclaims follow-up work that the evidence does not support. The transcript shows `/bin/bash: line 1: dylint.toml: command not found`, and the printed commit body still says `Let downstream workspaces mute specific lints from  instead of scattering...`, so the quoting issue was not fixed in the committed message. It also claims a napkin note was folded in, but the later `TOOL edit` on `.agent/napkin.md` failed (`Could not find the exact text...`), and `.agent/napkin.md` is not among the committed paths.

The OpenSpec delta now requires per-lint severity behavior that the code does not implement. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/specs/documentation/spec.md` adds required support/scenarios for `[tigerstyle.lint_levels]`, invalid-value warnings, overlap warnings, and allow/warn/deny behavior, but `src/config.rs` only adds `disabled_lints`, and `src/lib.rs` only gates registration with `cfg.lint_is_disabled(...)`; there is no `lint_levels` field, validation, normalization, or registration-time level override logic in the reviewed diff.

The implementation does not follow the design’s “shared lint-name inventory” decision and instead creates another hand-maintained source of truth. `src/lib.rs` adds `const KNOWN_LINTS: &[&str] = &[...]` for validation, while registration still repeats lint names in separate `if !cfg.lint_is_disabled("...")` blocks. `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/design.md` Decision 5 says config validation and registration should derive names from one shared inventory.

The response asserts concrete repo-state details that are not supported by the supplied evidence: “`main` ahead 1,” “only dirty file is `.agent/review-metrics.jsonl`,” “No half-done uncommitted code,” and “other active changes are 0/N.” In the provided transcript, there is no `git status`, branch, or active-change listing output; the only direct filesystem evidence is the current diff showing `.agent/review-metrics.jsonl` changed. That makes part of the ROI justification unverified.

`openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md` marks `Add validation: warn on unknown lint names at load time` as done, but the implementation shown in `src/config.rs` only validates `disabled_lints`. The new `warn_unknown_disabled_lints` method iterates `self.disabled_lints` only, and `load()` only calls that method. The change still has no `lint_levels` field or unknown-name handling for it, even though the spec requirement says there must be “a warning (not error) for unknown lint names in config.”

The completion report overclaims a file change outside the reviewed diff. It says `.agent/napkin.md` was updated, but the supplied `Git Status` and diff only show modifications to `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md`, `src/config.rs`, and `src/lib.rs`.

The completion report claims `cargo test --lib` and `cargo test --test ui -- --ignored --nocapture` passed, but the supplied evidence includes no transcript or tool output for either command. The only concrete verification output shown is `openspec_gate`. For a refactor of `src/lib.rs` registration wiring, the claimed test pass is not reviewable from the supplied evidence.

Missing a task to capture reviewable verification evidence for the new test/workflow claims. Evidence: the last user prompt says there was "No supplied evidence for the claimed cargo test --lib and UI test runs." In `openspec/changes/per-lint-configuration/tasks.md`, Phase 4 includes `Verify config changes in nix flake check and the targeted UI fixture gate...`, but there is no explicit task to save command lines/transcripts/artifacts for the Phase 1/2 unit and integration tests or the custom UI harness runs.
